Name of the Surah

It is called Az-Zumar (The Groups), because Allah Most High mentions in it the groups of the blessed, who are the people of Paradise, and the groups of the wretched, who are the people of the Fire.

Some of the Surah's Objectives

• Mention of one of the doubts of the polytheists regarding their worship of idols besides Allah, and the refutation of that doubt, and the negation of a form of shirk, namely their claim that Allah, glory be to Him, has a son, and the argument against them from their own actions, namely their turning to Allah when harm befalls them.

• Explanation of the proofs and evidences for the Oneness of the Lord of the worlds: in the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of the night and the day, the subjugation of the sun and the moon, the wondrous creation of man, and the creation of livestock and their variety. All of these are clear proofs of Allah's power and Oneness, which demand gratitude, not denial.

• The Messenger ﷺ is directed to proclaim the pure word of Tawhid (Monotheism), and to declare his fear of disobeying Allah and his determination to follow His method. There is also a comparison between the state of the polytheists and the state of the sincere believers devoted to Allah, and an illustration of the condition of both groups in this world and the Hereafter.

• Extolling the status of the Qur'an, that it is sent down from Allah, and the call to reflect and ponder upon it.

• Explanation of the difference between one who worships Allah and one who worships other deities, and informing the polytheists that they and their partners are of no account with Allah or with His Messenger ﷺ. There is also a debate with them about the falsehood of their supposed gods, and a warning that there may befall them what befell the polytheists of earlier nations, and an explanation of the enormity of shirk and the warning against it, and that it nullifies all deeds.

• Description of the Day of Resurrection, and explanation of the state of the believers who affirm the truth and of the disbelievers who deny it.

[Tafsir]

The revelation of the Qur'an is only from Allah, the Mighty in His power and His retribution, the Wise in His governance and His rulings.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 2:

We have sent down to you, O Messenger, the Qur'an, which enjoins the truth and justice. So worship Allah alone, and devote all your religion sincerely to Him.

Verily, to Allah alone belongs complete obedience, free from any association with Him (shirk). As for those who associated others with Allah and took protectors besides Him, they said: "We worship those deities only so that they may intercede for us with Allah and bring us closer to Him in rank." Thus they disbelieved by this, because worship and intercession belong to Allah alone. Indeed Allah will judge between the believers who were sincere and those who associated others with Allah on the Day of Resurrection concerning what they differed about in their worship, and He will recompense each according to what he deserves. Indeed Allah does not guide to the straight path one who is a liar against Allah, a persistent disbeliever in His signs and proofs.

If God had wished to take a son, He would have chosen whatever He willed from His creation. Exalted is God and sanctified above having a son. He is the One, the Unique, the Self-Sufficient Lord (al-Samad), the Subduer who has overpowered His creation by His might, so everything submits to Him in humble subjection.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 39, verse 5:

God created the heavens and the earth and what is in them with truth. He causes the night to enter upon the day and the day to enter upon the night, and He subjected the sun and the moon with regularity for the benefit of His servants. Each of them runs in its orbit until the Hour is established. Surely, God, who performed these deeds and bestowed these blessings upon His creation, is the Mighty over His creation, the Forgiving of the sins of His repentant servants.

Your Lord created you, O people, from Adam, and created from him his spouse. And He brought into being for you eight kinds of livestock, males and females: of camels, cattle, sheep and goats. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, stage after stage of creation, within three darknesses: the darkness of the belly, the womb, and the placenta. That is Allah, who created these things, your Lord, the One who alone possesses dominion, the One who alone deserves worship. How, then, do you turn away from worshipping Him to worshipping others of His creation?

If you disbelieve, O people, in your Lord, and do not believe in Him, nor follow His messengers, then indeed He is Free of need from you; He has no need of you, while you are the ones in need of Him. He is not pleased with disbelief for His servants, nor does He command them to it; rather, He is pleased for them to be grateful for His blessings upon them. No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you did and call you to account for it. Indeed, He is All-Knowing of the secrets of souls and what the breasts conceal.

When affliction, hardship, or illness befalls a person, he remembers his Lord and cries out to Him and calls upon Him. Then, when He answers him, removes his harm from him, and bestows His blessings upon him, he forgets his supplication to his Lord when he was in need of Him, and associates others with Him, in order to lead others astray from faith in God and obedience to Him. Say to him, O Messenger, threatening him: Enjoy your disbelief for a little while, until your death and the end of your term. Indeed, you are among the people of the Fire, who will abide therein forever.

Is one who is an unbeliever, enjoying his disbelief, better, or one who worships his Lord and is obedient to Him, spending the hours of the night standing and prostrating before Allah, fearing the punishment of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say, O Messenger: Are those who know their Lord and the true religion equal to those who know nothing of that? They are not equal. Only those of sound minds take heed and recognize the difference.

Say, O Prophet: "O My servants who believe in Allah and His Messenger, fear your Lord by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience. For those who do good in this world by worshipping their Lord and obeying Him, there is a good reward in the Hereafter, which is Paradise, and a good reward in this world, such as health, provision, victory, and other things. And the earth of Allah is spacious, so migrate within it to wherever you can worship your Lord and establish your religion." Indeed, those who are patient are given their reward in the Hereafter without measure, without counting, and without limit, and this is a magnification of the reward and recompense of the patient.

Say, O Messenger, to the people: Indeed, God has commanded me and those who follow me to devote worship sincerely to Him alone, to the exclusion of anything else. He has commanded me to be the first to submit among my community, so I submit to Him in tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), I devote my worship sincerely to Him, and I disavow every deity other than Him.

Say, O Messenger, to the people: "Indeed, I fear that if I disobey my Lord in what He has commanded me, namely worshipping Him and devoting my obedience sincerely to Him, I will suffer the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, the day whose terror is great."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verses 14–15:

As for you, [O polytheists], worship whatever you wish besides Allah, of idols, images, and other of His creatures; it will not harm me in the least." This is a threat and a warning to whoever worships other than Allah and associates others with Him. Say, [O Messenger]: "Truly, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection," and that is by misguiding them in this world and turning them away from faith. Verily, the loss of these polytheists, of themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, is the clear and manifest loss.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 17–18:

As for those who avoid obedience to Satan and the worship of other than God, and who turn back to God in worship and in sincere devotion to Him, theirs is good news in the life of this world, in the form of good praise and divine success from God, and in the Hereafter, God's good pleasure and everlasting bliss in Paradise. So give good news, O Prophet, to My servants who listen to speech and follow the best of it. The best and most rightly guiding speech is the Word of God, then the words of His Messenger (ﷺ). Those are the ones whom God has guided to right direction and steadfastness, and has led to the best of morals and deeds; and those are the people of sound minds.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 17–18:

Those are the ones whom God has guided to right direction and steadfastness, and has led to the best of morals and deeds; and those are the people of sound minds.

Is it he upon whom the word of punishment has been justified—by his persistence in his error and obstinacy—so there is no way for you, O Messenger, to guide him? Can you, then, save the one who is in the Fire? You are not able to do that.

But those who feared their Lord, by obeying Him and sincerely worshipping Him, will have in Paradise elevated chambers built one above another, with rivers flowing beneath their chambers and dwellings. Allah has promised this to His God-fearing servants as a promise that will certainly be fulfilled, for Allah does not break His promise.

Have you not seen, O Messenger, that Allah sends down water from the clouds and makes it flow into the earth as springs, and channels it as running streams? Then through this water He brings forth crops of varying colors and kinds. Then it withers after its greenness and freshness, so you see it turned yellow, and then He makes it into debris, crumbled and broken into pieces? Indeed, in that act of Allah there is a reminder and an admonition for people of sound minds.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 22:

Is one whom Allah has expanded his breast for Islam, so that he rejoices in accepting it, submitting to it and believing in it, and who is upon clear insight into his affair and guidance from his Lord, [equal to one who is not like that?] They are not equal. Woe and destruction to those whose hearts have hardened and turned away from the remembrance of Allah; those are in clear error, far from the truth.

God Almighty is the One who sent down the most beautiful discourse (ahsan al-hadith), which is the Great Qur'an, resembling itself in its beauty, its perfection, and its freedom from contradiction. Within it, stories, rulings, proofs, and clear evidences are repeated, and its recitation is repeated without the reader growing weary of its frequent repetition. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at hearing it, out of being affected by its warnings and threats; then their skins and hearts soften, out of joy at its promises and its encouragement. That being affected by the Qur'an is guidance from Allah to His servants. Allah guides through the Qur'an whomever He wills of His servants. And whomever Allah leaves astray from faith in this Qur'an, because of his disbelief and obstinacy, has no guide to direct him or grant him success.

Is one who will be thrown into the Fire, bound in shackles (so that he cannot protect himself from the Fire except with his face, because of his disbelief and misguidance) better, or one who will enjoy the Garden because God has guided him? And it will be said on that Day to the wrongdoers: "Taste the consequence of what you used to earn in the world of disobedience to God."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verses 25–26:

Those who came before your people, O Messenger, denied their messengers, so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive its coming. If these polytheists only knew that what befell those (nations) was because of their disbelief and their denial, they would take heed.

God has struck a parable: a slave owned by several partners who are quarreling, so he is bewildered in trying to please them, and a slave devoted wholly to one master who knows his wishes and what pleases him. Are the two equal in comparison? They are not equal. Likewise, the polytheist is in bewilderment and doubt, while the believer is at ease and in tranquility. All perfect praise belongs to God alone; but most of the polytheists do not know the truth, so they do not follow it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 30–31:

Indeed you, O Messenger, will die, and they too will die. Then on the Day of Resurrection, all of you, O people, will dispute before your Lord, and He will judge between you with justice and fairness.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 30–31:

Indeed you, O Messenger, will die, and they too will die. Then on the Day of Resurrection, all of you, O people, will dispute before your Lord, and He will judge between you with justice and fairness.

There is no one more wrong-doing than the one who fabricates a lie against God: by attributing to Him what does not befit Him, such as partners and offspring, or by claiming, "I have been inspired," when nothing was inspired to him. And there is no one more wrong-doing than the one who denies the truth that was sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ). Is there not in the Fire a dwelling and an abode for the one who disbelieves in God, does not affirm Muhammad (ﷺ), and does not act upon what he brought? Yes indeed.

He who brought the truth in his words and deeds, from among the prophets and their followers, and who affirmed it through faith and action: these are the ones who combined the qualities of piety (taqwa). At the forefront of these is the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers, Muhammad (ﷺ), and the believers who followed him and acted upon his law (shari'ah) from among the Companions (Sahabah), may Allah be pleased with them, and then those who came after them until the Day of Judgment.

They will have whatever they wish in the presence of their Lord, of all kinds of pleasures and desired things. That is the reward of one who obeyed his Lord with true obedience and worshipped Him with true worship.

So that Allah may expiate for them the worst of the deeds they did in this world, because of their repentance and turning back to Him from the evil deeds they committed therein, and Allah will reward them for their obedience in this world with the best of what they used to do, which is Paradise.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 36:

﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ — meaning Muhammad (ﷺ) — ﴿And they threaten you with those other than Him.﴾ — and the disbelievers' threats and their plotting, lest they reach him with harm? And whoever Allah grants success to believe in Him, act by His Book, and follow His Messenger, then no one can lead him astray from the truth he is upon. Is not Allah Almighty in His retribution against the disbelievers among His creation, and against those who disobey Him?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 38:

If you (O Messenger) were to ask these polytheists who worship other than Allah, "Who created the heavens and the earth?", they would surely say, "Allah created them." Thus they acknowledge the Creator. Say to them: Can these deities that you associate with Allah remove from me a harm that Allah has decreed for me, or dispel a distress that has befallen me? And can they withhold a benefit that Allah has facilitated for me, or restrain Allah's mercy from me? They will say, "They cannot do that." Say to them: Allah is sufficient for me and enough for me; upon Him rely those who depend on Him for securing their interests and warding off their harms. So He alone, in whose hand is all sufficiency, is my sufficiency, and He will suffice me for everything that concerns me.

Say, [O Messenger], to your obstinate people: "Continue acting in your state, which you have accepted for yourselves, since you worship what does not deserve to be worshipped and has no share in any affair. Indeed, I am acting in accordance with what I have been commanded: devoting worship to Allah alone in my words and deeds. So you will soon know who will be overtaken by a punishment that humiliates him in the worldly life, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment in the Hereafter that will neither turn away from him nor cease."

Indeed, We have sent down to you, O Messenger, the Qur'an with truth, as guidance for the worlds, to the path of right guidance. So whoever is guided by its light, acts upon what it contains, and remains steadfast upon its method, the benefit of that returns to himself. And whoever goes astray after the guidance has become clear to him, its harm returns only upon himself, and he will not harm Allah at all. And you, O Messenger, are not a guardian over them, to safeguard their deeds, to hold them accountable for them, or to compel them to what you wish. Your duty is only to convey (the message).

Allah, glory be to Him, is the One who takes the souls at the time of their death, and this is the greater death, the death by the expiry of the term. And He takes the soul of the one who has not died in his sleep, and this is the lesser death. So He withholds the soul of the one on whom death has decreed, which is the soul of the one who has died, and He sends the other soul back until it completes its term and its provision, and that is by returning it to the body of its owner. Indeed, in Allah's taking the souls of the dead and the sleeper, and His sending the soul of the sleeper and withholding the soul of the dead, are clear signs of Allah's power for those who reflect and contemplate.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 39, verse 43:

Or have these polytheists taken, besides Him, their gods that they worship as intercessors, to intercede for them with God regarding their needs? Say, O Messenger, to them: Do you take them as intercessors, as you claim, even though these gods own nothing and do not understand your worship of them?

Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists: "All intercession belongs to Allah. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. The matter entirely belongs to Allah alone, and none will intercede with Him except by His permission and His approval of the one for whom intercession is made. He is the One who possesses the heavens and the earth and disposes of them. So it is obligatory that intercession be sought from the One who owns it, and that worship be made sincerely for Him alone, and that it not be sought from these deities that neither harm nor benefit. Then to Him you will be returned after your death, for reckoning and recompense."

When God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter and in resurrection after death recoil in aversion; but when those other than Him are mentioned, such as idols, images, and saints, behold, they rejoice, because polytheism (shirk) agrees with their desires.

Say, "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Who created them without any prior example, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ regarding what was said about You, and about Your greatness, Your sovereignty, and belief in You and Your Messenger. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth about which they have differed, for You guide whom You will to a straight path."

And this was from the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ), and it is a teaching for the servants to resort to Allah, and to call upon Him by His Most Beautiful Names and His Exalted Attributes.

If the polytheists had everything on earth in wealth and treasures, and the like of it doubled along with it, they would surrender it all on the Day of Resurrection in order to ransom themselves from the evil of the punishment. Yet even if they surrendered it and ransomed themselves with it, it would not be accepted from them, nor would it avail them anything against the punishment of God. And there would appear to them on that Day, from God's command and His punishment, what they never reckoned in the world would befall them.

On the Day of Reckoning, the consequences of the evil deeds these deniers committed will appear to them. They ascribed to God what is not befitting of Him, committed sins during their lives, and a painful punishment will surround them from every side. This is a punishment for their mockery of the warning of punishment that the Messenger used to promise them, which they did not heed.

When affliction and hardship touch a person, he calls upon his Lord to relieve him. But when We remove from him what afflicted him and grant him a blessing from Us, he turns away from his Lord as a disbeliever, ungrateful for His favour, and says: "This has been given to me only because of knowledge from God that I am deserving and worthy of it." Rather, it is a trial by which God tests His servants, to see who will give thanks and who will deny. But most of them, through their ignorance and bad assumptions, do not know that this is a gradual leading-on (istidraj) from God and a test for them regarding gratitude for blessings.
Those before them among the earlier disbelieving nations said this same saying, but what they had earned of wealth and children did not avail them when the punishment came upon them.

Then the people of the earlier nations who said this same saying were struck by the evil consequences of the bad deeds they had earned, so they were hastened to disgrace in the life of this world. As for those among your own people, O Messenger, who wronged themselves and said this same saying, the evil consequences of what they earned will likewise strike them, just as it struck those before them. And they cannot escape Allah or outrun Him.

Have these people not known that God's provision to a human being does not indicate the good condition of its recipient? Indeed, God, in His perfect wisdom, expands provision for whomever He wills among His servants, whether righteous or wicked, and restricts it for whomever He wills among them. Indeed, in that expansion and restriction of provision there are clear signs for a people who affirm the command of God and act upon it.

Say, [O Messenger], to My servants who have transgressed against themselves by excess in sin, committing what their souls have led them to of wrongdoing: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins for whoever repents from them and turns away from them, no matter what they are. Indeed, He is the Forgiving of the sins of His repentant servants, the Merciful toward them.
And return to your Lord, O people, in obedience and repentance, and submit to Him before His punishment befalls you, after which no one will help you against Allah.

Follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord, which is the Great Qur'an, and all of it is good. So comply with its commands and avoid its prohibitions, before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you are unaware of it.

Obey your Lord and turn to Him in repentance, before a soul is seized with regret and says, "Alas for my loss over what I neglected in the world, of acting on what God commanded, and of falling short in His obedience and in what is due to Him. Indeed, I was in the world among those who mocked God's command, His Book, His Messenger, and the believers in Him."
Or [they] say: "If only Allah had guided me to His religion, I would have been among the righteous, those who avoid shirk and sins."

Or it might say, when it sees God's punishment encompassing it on the Day of Reckoning: "If only I had a return to the life of this world, so that I would be among those who did good by obeying their Lord and acting upon what the messengers commanded them."

The matter is not as you say. My clear signs, which point to the truth, have already come to you, but you denied them, grew arrogant and refused to accept and follow them, and you were among the disbelievers in God and His messengers.

On the Day of Resurrection, you will see those deniers who described their Lord in a way unbefitting Him, and attributed to Him partners and offspring, their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a dwelling and abode for whoever was arrogant toward God and refused to affirm His oneness and obey Him? Yes.

And Allah will save from Hell and its torment those who were mindful of their Lord by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, with their success and the fulfilment of their hope, which is attaining Paradise. No harm from the torment of Hell will touch them, nor will they grieve over what they missed of the pleasures of this world.
God Most High is the Creator of all things, their Lord, their Sovereign, and the One who disposes of them. He is over all things Guardian (Hafiz), managing all the affairs of His creation.

God holds the keys to the treasures of the heavens and the earth; He gives to His creation from them however He wills. As for those who denied the signs of the Qur'an and the clear proofs contained in it, they are the losers: in this world, by being forsaken from faith, and in the Hereafter, by their abiding forever in the Fire.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 64:

Say, (O Messenger), to the polytheists of your people: "Is it other than Allah, you ignorant ones concerning Allah, that you order me to worship, when worship is fit for nothing besides Him?"

And indeed it has been revealed to you, O Messenger, and to those before you among the Messengers: "If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers, those who have lost their religion and their Hereafter." This is because no righteous deed is accepted alongside shirk.
Rather, worship Allah alone, O Prophet, making your worship sincerely for Him alone with no partner, and be among those who give thanks to Allah for His blessings.

This is a commentary on the Qur'an, so I'll translate it as the passage stands.

The idolaters did not magnify Allah with the magnification due to Him, for they worshipped alongside Him others that can neither benefit nor harm, thereby equating a created being in its helplessness with the Creator, the Mighty, whose great power is such that the whole earth is in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens are folded up in His right hand. Exalted and magnified is He, glorified be He and exalted, above what these idolaters associate with Him. And in the verse is evidence for affirming the grip (qabḍah), the right hand (yamīn), and the folding (ṭayy) for Allah, as befits His majesty and greatness, without asking how (takyīf) and without likening (tashbīh).

And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will die, except those whom Allah wills to be spared from death. Then the angel will blow it a second time, announcing the resurrection of all creatures for reckoning before their Lord, and behold, they will be standing up from their graves, looking to see what Allah will do with them.

And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah, exalted is He, manifests Himself to His creatures to judge between them; the books of deeds of every individual will be laid open; and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward to testify against the nations. Allah will question the prophets about their conveying of the message and about what their peoples answered them with, and the Muslim nation, the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), will be brought as witnesses to testify to the conveying of the earlier messengers to their nations when those nations deny that the message was conveyed; thus the proof will be established against the nations. The Lord of the worlds will judge between the servants with perfect justice, and they will not be wronged in anything, neither by a reduction in reward nor by an increase in punishment.

The commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 70:

Allah pays every soul in full the reward for its deeds, whether good or evil, and He, glorified and exalted, is best aware of what they do in this world, whether obedience or disobedience.

And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them: "Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day?" They will say: "Yes, but the word of punishment has come due against the disbelievers."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 39, verse 72:

It is said to the deniers, that Allah is the true God, as humiliation and degradation for them: "Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever." So evil is the destination of those who were arrogant toward faith in Allah and toward acting by His law.

Those who had feared their Lord by affirming His oneness and acting in obedience to Him will be led to the Garden in groups. When they reach it, and its gates have been opened for them by their being granted entry, the angels appointed over the Garden will welcome them and greet them with joy and delight, because they are pure from the traces of sin, saying to them: "Peace be upon you. You are safe from every affliction; your conditions are good. So enter the Garden, abiding in it forever."

The believers will say: "All praise is due to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us, the promise He made to us through His messengers, and who has given us inheritance of the Garden, where we may settle wherever we wish. How excellent is the reward of those who do good, who strove in obedience to their Lord."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 39, verse 75:

And you see, O Prophet, the angels surrounding the Throne of the Most Merciful, glorifying their Lord above everything that is not befitting to Him. Allah, glorified and exalted, has judged between the creatures with truth and justice, so He has made the people of faith dwell in Paradise and the people of disbelief dwell in the Fire. It was also said: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, for what He has decreed between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire," a praise of bounty and grace, and a praise of justice and wisdom.
